cards.text: Some time later, Nahash, king of the Ammonites, dies, and his son takes over. Now David, king of Israel, has some history with Nahash. And David's about to make a move.

cards.question: Nahash once showed David kindness. Now that Nahash is gone, what does David say he'll show Nahash's son Hanun?

answers.text: Kindness
Caution
Strength

cards.question: David wants to reach out to Hanun after his father's death. How does he do it?

answers.text: He sends messengers to comfort him
He goes to the funeral himself
He writes him a letter of peace

cards.text: David's servants arrive in the land of the Ammonites to comfort Hanun. But Hanun's princes get to him first, and friend, they've got a THEORY.

cards.question: Hanun's princes don't believe David's servants came to comfort him. What do the princes say they really came to do?

answers.text: Spy out the land and overthrow it
Steal the royal treasure for David
Take Hanun back as a prisoner

cards.question: Hanun goes along with his princes. What does he do to David's servants?

answers.text: Shaves their beards and cuts their garments
Throws them into his prison
Sends them home with gifts

cards.text: David sends a sympathy card, and they read it like a ransom note. These men came to comfort a grieving son and left looking like they lost a fight with a paper shredder.
When someone tells David what happened, he sends messengers out to meet his men. They've been thoroughly humiliated.

cards.question: David has a message for his humiliated men. What does he tell them to do?

answers.text: Stay in Jericho until their beards grow back
Come straight home to Jerusalem right away
Go back to Hanun and demand an apology

cards.text: Over in Ammon, Hanun and the Ammonites realize they've become a stench to David. Friend, that is NOT a smell you can bake over.

cards.question: The Ammonites know David is not happy with them. What do they do about it?

answers.text: Hire chariots and horsemen from Aram
Send David a royal apology
Move their people out of the cities

cards.question: To pay for their hired army, the Ammonites send a thousand talents of ___.

answers.text: silver
gold
bronze

cards.text: That's not an apology, friend, that's a down payment on a war: thirty-two thousand chariots, plus the king of Maacah and his troops. They camp near Medeba while the Ammonites gather from their cities and march out for battle.

cards.question: David hears that the Ammonites and their hired army are marching out. What does David do?

answers.text: Sends his commander Joab with the mighty men
Hides his whole army inside Jerusalem
Sends Hanun a peace offering of silver

cards.text: The Ammonites line up at the entrance to their city, and the kings they hired wait out in the open country. Joab looks around and sees battle lines in front of him AND behind him.

cards.question: Joab has an enemy army in front of him and another behind him. How does he handle it?

answers.text: He splits his troops into two groups
He orders his troops to retreat
He waits for David to come help

cards.question: Joab takes the best men against the Ammonites and leaves his brother Abishai to face the Arameans.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Two brothers, two armies, one plan. Before the fighting starts, Joab tells Abishai exactly how this is gonna work.

cards.question: What's the deal Joab makes with his brother Abishai before the battle?

answers.text: If one side is losing the other comes to help
If one side is losing both fall back to Jerusalem
Whichever side wins first gets all the plunder

cards.question: Joab tells Abishai to be strong and fight bravely for their people and the cities of their God. Who does Joab leave the outcome to?

answers.text: The LORD
King David
The mighty men

cards.question: Joab and his troops advance to fight the Arameans. What do the Arameans do?

answers.text: They flee
They surrender
They charge

cards.question: When the Ammonites see the Arameans flee, they stand their ground and fight Abishai.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: ALL that silver, and the hired help is the first one out the door! The Ammonites run into their city, and Joab heads back to Jerusalem.
But the Arameans aren't finished. They've been beaten by Israel, so they send messengers to bring more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates.

cards.question: More Arameans are coming from beyond the Euphrates. Who leads them?

answers.text: Shophach the commander of Hadadezer's army
Abner the commander of Saul's army
Hanun the king of the Ammonites

cards.question: Word of the new Aramean army reaches David. What does David do this time?

answers.text: Gathers all Israel and crosses the Jordan
Sends Abishai out with half the army
Waits for them behind the city walls

cards.text: No more sending somebody else. The king himself lines up for battle, and the Arameans fight him.

cards.question: David and the Arameans are locked in battle. How does it end?

answers.text: The Arameans flee and Shophach is killed
The Arameans win and David pulls back
Both armies pull back with no winner

cards.text: David kills seven thousand of their charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers. The people under Hadadezer, the Aramean king these troops served, see that Israel has beaten them.

cards.question: Hadadezer's subjects have been defeated by Israel. What do they do now?

answers.text: Make peace with David and serve him
Send their chariots to help Hanun
Pull back and plan another attack

cards.question: After making peace with David, the Arameans are still willing to help the Ammonites.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: In the spring, the time when kings march out to war, Joab leads the army out and ravages the land of the Ammonites. And the Arameans? Phone's on Do Not Disturb.

cards.question: This time, David rides out to war right alongside Joab.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: Joab reaches the Ammonite city of Rabbah and besieges it. How does the siege end?

answers.text: Joab attacks Rabbah and demolishes it
Joab gives up and heads back home
Rabbah holds out and Joab moves on

cards.text: Then David takes the crown right off the head of their king. And friend, this is NOT a crown from a party store.

cards.question: The crown weighs a talent of ___ and is set with precious stones.

answers.text: gold
silver
bronze

cards.question: David takes that heavy crown from the Ammonite king. Where does it end up?

answers.text: On David's own head
Back on their king's head
Locked away in Rabbah

cards.text: A talent of gold on his head, plus a great amount of plunder from the city. Friend, I wear a chef's hat and MY neck gets tired.

cards.question: Rabbah has fallen. What does David do with the people who were there?

answers.text: Puts them to work with saws and axes
Sends them away to live in Jericho
Brings them all back to Jerusalem

cards.question: David does the same thing in all the other Ammonite cities.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then David and all his troops head home to Jerusalem. And THAT, friend, is how a sympathy card read like a ransom note turned into a whole war.

findings.problem: The card cites only 1 Chronicles 19:1, but it also tells that David 'has some history with Nahash.' That comes from 19:2, where Nahash showed kindness to David. The citation is narrower than the verses the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It only jokes about 19:3-4, which cards 4, 5 and 6 already covered, so it is a recap card. Its paper-shredder line also laughs at how the humiliated servants look rather than at their situation.
Hadadezer first appears here, inside the right answer 'Shophach the commander of Hadadezer's army,' and nothing says who he is. He isn't introduced until stop 2, card 15.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Send their chariots to help Hanun' is not false everywhere in the passage. In 19:6-7, the Ammonites hired chariots from Zobah and Aram, which means Arameans, including Zobah, Hadadezer's kingdom, did send chariots to help Hanun earlier in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
